correctness.rationale: In the seedless d-regular tree (fixed d>=3) with atomless independent arrival marks and unbiased independent tie rankings, a specified nonbacktracking k-edge ancestry segment requires strictly decreasing marks. The path-local probability is h_(d-1)(t0)prod_i h_(d-2)(ti), h_m(t)=E[1/(1+Bin(m,t))]. Disjoint side-neighbor sets permit exact multiplication and give the double-integral tail formula. With F(t)=int_0^t h_(d-2), b=H_(d-1)/(d-1), change x=F(s),y=F(t) concentrates (y-x)^(k-1) at x=0,y=b, producing P(L>=k)=b H_(d-1)^k/(k+1)!*(1+O_d(1/k)). Packing vertices at distances>2k gives independent local events and N_R^(1-o(1)) trials; summable union bounds and Borel-Cantelli prove the a.s. M_R scale. Independent exact low-k checks d3 (3/4,31/90,31/252) and d4 corroborate.
